agents.auc: AUC0-24 266.6 ug-eq*h/g (plasma, Table 2); AUC0-inf 548 ug*h/mL and AUC0-t 267 ug*h/mL (RESULTS text)
agents.pk_quote: RESULTS: 'Plasma radioactivity t1/2 was approximately 22 h. With greater than half of the AUC0-inf of 548 μg•h/mL extrapolated beyond 24 h (AUC0-t 267 μg•h/mL), the estimated total body clearance was 27.4 mL/h/kg, with a steady-state distribution volume of 936 mL/kg.' DISCUSSION explicitly names the phase: 'The 22 h terminal half-life of plasma radioactivity is, therefore, likely not the true terminal half-life, which would only be revealed with much longer sampling.' Cmax and Tmax are taken from the Table 2 'Pseudo-PK parameters' block, plasma column: Tmax (min) 5 and Cmax 47.0±16.7. Note the Table 2 Cmax row header reads '(μg-eq/g)' while the plasma column header reads '(μg-q/mL)'; the plasma parameter is a per-mL concentration, so the column header and the body units (8-11 μg equivalents of WLBU2/ml plasma) were used rather than the row header. Non-compartmental analysis with PK Solutions 2.0. Tissue pseudo-PK values are also tabulated (e.g. liver Cmax 117±4 μg-eq/g at Tmax 30 min, kidney 129±12 μg-eq/g at 15 min, spleen 92.0±20.3 μg-eq/g at 120 min, lung 47.3±8.2 μg-eq/g at 5 min, brain 3.30±0.20 μg-eq/g at 960 min).

notes: IMPORTANT INTERPRETIVE CAVEAT stated by the authors: these are total-14C 'pseudo-pharmacokinetic' parameters, not parameters for intact WLBU2. The DISCUSSION states 'The pseudo-pharmacokinetic parameters of 14C content are a composite of the underlying individual parameters of the respective analytes with the 14C label. The 22 h terminal half-life of plasma radioactivity is, therefore, likely not the true terminal half-life, which would only be revealed with much longer sampling.' Roughly 34% of the dose was unaccounted for at 24 h and is attributed to expiration of 14CO2 after cleavage to the 14C-valine label. Parameters were derived by non-compartmental analysis from average concentration values using PK Solutions 2.0; only a terminal/elimination half-life is reported, and no absorption phase or absorption half-life is described (dosing was intravenous). Unit-header inconsistency in Table 2: the Cmax and AUC0-24 row labels carry per-gram units while the plasma column is per-mL; the parameter names and body text were used to assign plasma Cmax = 47.0±16.7 ug-eq/mL and plasma AUC0-24 = 266.6 ug-eq*h/g as printed. There is also an internal inconsistency on the single-dose MTD: the ABSTRACT says 20 mg/kg while the RESULTS body says 'The IV single dose MTD for WLBU2 is 30 mg/kg' and the DISCUSSION says 'The murine IV single dose, and daily x 5 MTD for WLBU2 were 30 and 15 mg/kg, respectively'; the body values are used here. Control plasma and control lung/liver/kidney homogenates were spiked with [14C]-WLBU2 or WLBU2 as bioanalytical recovery controls; these are method-validation steps rather than a biological ex vivo assay, so no ex vivo study type is claimed. An untreated (no injection) control group was included in the multiple-dose MTD study; it receives no substance and is therefore not listed as an agent.
